text:
maria: quick design thread — prototyping a couple of new behaviours for the routing policies editor: priority pinning, bulk-reorder mode, and a compact rule list view. posting early so we can catch a11y and copy nits. mock: https://mock.redwood/dev/policy-pin-bulk.gif

jared: looks promising. two immediate UX asks: 1) when a rule is pinned it should visually detach from the stack (small pinned chip + subtle shadow) so users understand it's anchored. 2) bulk-reorder mode needs an affordance that makes it obvious how to exit.

zeynep: accessibility thoughts: pinned items must still be reachable in tab order and announced. consider `aria-roledescription=\"pinned rule\"` and announce with `aria-live=polite` when pin/unpin occurs: "Rule X pinned". Also ensure pinned rules can be re-ordered among themselves and that SRs hear the new index.

kevin: contrast/colour note: our pinned chip currently uses blue-300 which fails AA on small text. switch to blue-600 token or add a darker border. also add focus outline that meets 3:1 at least for touch targets.

sam: bulk-reorder mode: proposal — enter via a toolbar button "Bulk reorder" which converts cards to a compact dense list with keyboard-first controls (up/down handlers). show an in-panel help line: "Press Esc to exit". When exiting, automatically validate final order and show any blockers in a persistent banner.

maria: about validation — if the final order triggers policy conflicts, show inline cluster errors and a sticky toast in the left rail listing affected rules. Don't use ephemeral toasts for order-related errors. users may reorder then navigate away and lose context.

jared: agree. also add an undo snackbar after reorder with 10s window. "Undo" should restore previous order and re-run the simulation automatically.

zeynep: keyboard accessibility for bulk-reorder: support arrow keys to move focus, `M` to toggle move mode for a focused rule, and `Ctrl+ArrowUp/Down` as alternative. Announce movements: "Moved rule {title} to position {n}" via `aria-live=assertive` for clarity (since it's a direct user action). Debounce announcements if user is making many moves rapidly.

kevin: ensure modifiers are configurable; watch for platform conflicts. also add a preference: "Enable bulk reorder shortcuts" for teams who want to opt out.

sam: compact rule list view should reduce padding and hide secondary metadata but keep icons for type + validation. allow users to pin/unpin directly from compact view and support multi-select (shift+click) for group pin/unpin or move.

maria: multi-select is interesting. need clear selection state and keyboard multi-select semantics (Shift+Arrow to extend, Space to toggle). provide an accessible summary toolbar: "3 rules selected" with actions: Pin, Move to top, Move to bottom, Delete.

jared: copy tweak: change the left-rail CTA from "Simulate traffic" to "Run routing simulation" and for bulk actions use labels like "Move to top" rather than just chevrons. Be explicit.

zeynep: voiceover nit: when you open bulk-reorder mode, announce: "Bulk reorder mode activated. Use Arrow keys to navigate, M to toggle move mode, Esc to exit." Use `aria-modal` semantics for the mode so focus is constrained.

kevin: visual motion: when many rules move at once (multi-select reorder), avoid animating every card; instead use a single list-level animation to minimize motion for vestibular-sensitive users. include a reduced-motion preference.

sam: for preview simulation integration: add a small "Run preset" dropdown in the bulk-reorder toolbar so users can quickly test common scenarios after changing order. presets should be keyboard-accessible and announce results summary when complete.

maria: next steps: jared will mock pinned visual language + undo snackbar; zeynep will draft aria copy and announcer rules; kevin will run contrast checks and reduced-motion guidance; sam will prototype compact list + bulk actions and wire sample presets into the preview harness. i'll consolidate mock links and post a short walkthrough video later today. :thumbsup:

design-bot: Created task: "POLICY-UX: pinning + bulk-reorder + a11y validations" (EPIC-4201).

jared: one last prod note: when pinning across pages (if the list is paginated), we need to surface that pin persisted and show an indicator in the global rule index. Avoid surprises where pinned rules appear missing after pagination.

zeynep: store pin state in the policy config and treat it as part of the ordering payload so it survives exports/imports. also include it in the audit log messages.

kevin: I'll add these to the accessibility checklist: announcer messaging, focus trap for bulk mode, contrast tokens for pinned chips, reduced-motion path, keyboard multi-select semantics.

maria: thanks team. will update mocks and reopen thread for final pass.
